scope: 41 local Rust Duration, Instant duration and relative arithmetic dependencies. Implementation and requirement statuses unchanged.
source_comparison: Frozen Temporal proposal via durable checklist rows. ECMA-262 remains requested authority.

review_timing.scope: Patch and evidence assembly after initial source/proposal review.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §13.23 step 1: select the fixed clock-unit entry.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Maps clock DateTimeUnit variants to TimeUnit and leaves calendar/day units to their respective caller branches. This is typed unit-table selection.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §13.17 step 9: map a prepared singular or plural unit name.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Typed parser matches singular text after stripping the one plural suffix. Public option Get, conversion, unset and auto are separate contracts.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §13.17 step 9: retain the selected clock unit in typed settings.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Enum adapter widens TimeUnit to DateTimeUnit with the same unit. No option parsing or default selection.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §5.5.12 step 3: supply the plain clock remainder.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Default RelativeAnchor projection uses Euclidean within-day remainder. Zoned anchors override with the local clock adjusted by offset.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.5.33 steps 8.a, 9: delegate calendar window endpoint construction.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Forwards typed duration fields to the anchor endpoint owner. Plain/zoned calendar and range policies are selected by that owner.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §5.5.12 step 9: obtain the calendar date portion.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Selects the date largest unit, invokes provider date difference and copies year/month/week/day into the typed field record. Provider arithmetic is separately owned.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §5.5.12 steps 3–11: split an exact span into date and clock parts.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Plain branch compares exact within-day remainders and adjusts date by one day when signs conflict before calling calendar difference. Zoned branch has its own bounded correction loop; this mapping does not claim its wider window invariants.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.5.38 steps 5.a, 6.a, 7.a, 9.b: select typed rounding paths.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Separates calendar-unit nudge, zoned clock carry and fixed day/clock rounding after exact difference preparation. Rounds signed i128 spans and bubbles typed fields when needed. Final window, retry and provider premises stay in their individual checklist rows.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §13.14 steps 3–4: validate typed rounding caps and divisibility.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Checks order and input increment magnitude before selecting strict hour/minute/second/subsecond bounds. Date units skip clock cap. Public option ordering and defaults are separate.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.5.12 steps 3, 5–15: fill typed fields over zero defaults.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Uses a zero record and delegates prepared optional fields to with_fields. JS receiver/bag reads and property conversions are separate.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.3.15 steps 4–24: replace supplied typed duration fields.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Prepared optional fields replace corresponding stored values. Validates the result through new. Typed all-empty error backs the already-validated caller policy.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.5.16 steps 1–9: validate signs and normalized duration bounds.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Converts typed fields to stored Number-equivalent integers; rejects mixed signs, out-of-range calendar fields, and an excessive exact normalized time magnitude. Constructor realm, public integer coercion and JS slots remain external.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.3.22 steps 11.a, 14–18: prepare duration text at requested precision.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Retains original fields at unit quantum; otherwise rounds the exact clock sum, preserves calendar fields and balances the rounded span at the selected largest unit. Typed formatter validates the result and defers text writing.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.5.5 step 1: expose the existing typed duration field record.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Returns the stored array unchanged for consumers assembling internal date/time records. No JS slot or object allocation occurs in the accessor.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.5.13 steps 1–2: return the first nonzero field sign.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Reads typed fields from largest to smallest, stops at first nonzero, defaults to zero. Uniform nonzero sign is already an invariant.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.3.16 step 3: negate each typed duration field.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Maps exact sign negation over stored fields. Valid magnitude bounds and uniform sign are preserved. Public brand and result allocation are outside.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.3.17 step 3: take the magnitude of each duration field.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Applies exact integer absolute value to each stored field with the same bounds. No object conversion or new realm allocation.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.5.21 steps 1–7: combine clock units in exact nanoseconds.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Checked i128 multiplication and addition expand the clock-field fold. Optional day inclusion supplies the fixed-24-hour path. Exclusive magnitude guard reuses the stored timing invariant.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.5.8 steps 5–12: split typed nanoseconds into clock fields.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Checks input magnitude, divides from the selected largest clock factor with signed truncation, and retains the signed remainder. This is equivalent to decomposing magnitude then restoring sign before stored-field conversion.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.2.3 steps 5.a, 15–17: compare fixed duration spans.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Full typed equality returns Equal. Otherwise this no-anchor path rejects years/months/weeks and compares exact fixed-day and clock sums.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.3.21 step 14.d: total a fixed span in the selected clock unit.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Rejects calendar units without an anchor, sums fixed days and clock exactly, then divides once to the requested output Number.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.3.21 step 14.d: divide the exact fixed span by one day.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Typed day total shares fixed-span validation and exact rational projection with clock totals.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.3.20 steps 29–34: round and rebalance a fixed duration.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Rejects calendar fields/largest unit on this no-anchor route. Computes fixed-unit quantum, rounds exact sum, decomposes from requested largest unit and checks stored-field bounds.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.5.41 steps 3–11: add exact fixed spans and rebalance.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Rejects calendar fields without an anchor, selects the coarsest nonzero field across operands, adds fixed day/clock spans exactly and decomposes the validated sum.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.5.41 step 2: negate the second duration before addition.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Typed subtraction delegates field negation then invokes the same fixed-span add path. Public conversion of other happened before this wrapper.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.5.8 steps 5–10: select the typed decomposition start index.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Maps each clock unit to its field index used by the exact quotient/remainder loop. Does not itself compute field amounts.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.3.21 step 15: round the exact total ratio to Number once.
reviewed_rows.evidence: For bounded positive-divisor callers, computes integer exponent and significand, applies nearest/ties-even by comparing exact remainders, then assembles f64 bits. Numerator and shift bounds are separately proved.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §8.5.10 steps 4–7: add clock nanoseconds to the Instant.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Rejects date fields, adds exact clock nanoseconds to epoch and checks the resulting Instant range. Public Duration coercion is outside.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §8.5.10 step 2: negate the typed duration for Instant subtraction.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Delegates checked_add with negated duration fields before calculating the exact result epoch.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §8.5.9 steps 4–5: round the exact Instant difference.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Validates typed increment cap/divisibility, subtracts exact epochs, rounds the signed span and then decomposes clock fields. Does not read public settings.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §8.5.9 step 6: reverse the typed Instant difference for since.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Calls the same until arithmetic with swapped endpoints so the supplied rounding mode sees the desired signed span. Public since rounding option semantics remain caller-owned.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §13.37 steps 1–3, 23–44: scan and decode duration text.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Consumes ASCII designators in order, validates optional sign and terminal time-only decimal fraction, converts fraction exactly into lower units, then constructs the typed duration under stored-field bounds.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.5.40 steps 1–17: write duration sign, fields and fraction.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Emits nonzero fields in order, combines exact subseconds, writes required seconds for zero/fixed precision and applies automatic trailing-zero suppression. Input rounding is done before this writer.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.3.23 step 3: supply auto precision for typed duration display.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Rust Display calls the shared duration writer at automatic precision. This is typed renderer correspondence for the default profile, not a public JS toJSON call route.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.3.22 steps 11.a, 18: write the prepared duration and precision.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Delegates the typed value and prepared precision to the same writer regardless of how the formatter was created.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.5.27 steps 1–3: round exact nanoseconds and check the result bound.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Checks typed input magnitude and allowed quantum, delegates integer rounding and enforces the output time-duration limit before returning.

key.symbol: impl<Z: TimeZone + Clone + PartialEq, C: CalendarProvider> ZonedDateTime<Z, C>::total_duration

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.3.21 steps 12.e–f: add the duration and total the zoned span.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Uses constrained zoned addition then totals the exact endpoint. Zero clock-unit result can return directly; date units retain endpoint evaluation.

key.symbol: impl<Z: TimeZone + Clone + PartialEq, C: CalendarProvider> ZonedDateTime<Z, C>::round_duration

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.3.20 steps 27.e–f: form the zoned duration rounding target.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Checks the typed date-increment constraint, adds through the current provider and passes the exact destination to shared rounding. JS option reads and signed result construction remain external.

key.symbol: impl<Z: TimeZone + Clone + PartialEq, C: CalendarProvider> ZonedDateTime<Z, C>::compare_durations

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.2.3 steps 5.a, 12.c–g: compare zoned endpoints.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Exact field equality skips addition. Clock-only inputs compare as integer clock spans. If either record has date fields, compare two separately added constrained zoned endpoints.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.5.39 steps 1.b–c, 3: total the typed relative span.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Clock units divide exact epoch difference. Calendar totals derive a count and adjacent endpoint bracket, preserve endpoint checks and form the rational in integers. Window invariants remain separately scoped.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.5.38 step 5.a: round the retained week prefix or delegate.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Week-with-larger-calendar-unit branch keeps years/months, derives the week count and uses the exact endpoint span for rounding. Other routes delegate shared difference. Zero/equality and provider-bound proofs remain separate.

validation.result: 14 Bazel targets passed in the same validation batch.
